quizzes.title: Hydrogen Train: Specifications
quizzes.passage: India has flagged off its first indigenous hydrogen-powered train, which PM Modi inaugurated. The train is configured as a Hydrogen Fuel Cell Trainset, so hydrogen is the fuel at the centre of its design. The train operates on the Jind–Sonipat route, and its propulsion comes from a Hydrogen Fuel Cell Propulsion System. The launch is covered in the July 2026 current affairs section on Defence, Space and Science and Technology. The booklet presents the train under the heading Why in News, followed by a list of key highlights. These highlights describe the train's approved operational speed and its design speed, and they name the organisation that developed it. The booklet also lists the major components of the train, including fuel cells, batteries, a hydrogen storage system and motors. Each of these components has its own role in the working of the train. Hydrogen is written as H in the booklet, and it is described as a chemical element. The Practice Questions section that follows checks readers on the route, the design and the components of the train. The page carries the footer of a Jaipur-based current affairs publication, and the same section of the booklet also covers other developments in railways, which are discussed separately.

questions.q: In which state is the Jind–Sonipat route, on which India's first indigenous Hydrogen-powered Train was inaugurated?
questions.explanation: The booklet places the Jind–Sonipat route in Haryana.

questions.q: What is the atomic number of Hydrogen?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the atomic number of Hydrogen as 1.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the Universe's normal matter.
Reason (R): Hydrogen is the lightest chemical element.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are in the booklet, but being the lightest element does not explain why hydrogen is the most abundant.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells   ->   A. Convert electrical energy into mechanical energy
II. Lithium Iron Phosphate Batteries   ->   B. Generate electricity through an electrochemical reaction between hydrogen and oxygen
III. Hydrogen Storage System   ->   C. Store surplus electricity generated by fuel cells
IV. Electric Traction Motors   ->   D. Store compressed hydrogen in High-Pressure Cylinders
questions.explanation: Fuel cells generate electricity, batteries store surplus electricity, the storage system holds compressed hydrogen and the traction motors convert electrical into mechanical energy.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Jind–Sonipat route on which the train runs is 89 km long.
II. Lithium Iron Phosphate Batteries generate electricity through an electrochemical reaction.
III. The design speed of the train is 110 km/h.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while Statement II gives the fuel cells' function to the batteries.

questions.q: What percentage of the Universe's normal matter does Hydrogen constitute?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Hydrogen constitutes nearly 75% of the Universe's normal matter.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The train is configured as a 10-coach Hydrogen Fuel Cell Trainset.
II. Electric Traction Motors store surplus electricity generated by the fuel cells.
III. Hydrogen is the heaviest chemical element.
questions.explanation: Only Statement I is correct, since the motors do not store electricity and Hydrogen is the lightest element.

quizzes.title: Railway and S&T Developments
quizzes.passage: The July 2026 current affairs section covers several new developments in railways and science and technology. KAVACH is an indigenous safety system, and its features include centralised live monitoring of train movements and the relaying of SOS messages. The Vande Metro Train, which was India's first, has been given a new name. Namo Bharat/RapidX runs on the Delhi–Ghaziabad–Meerut corridor. Mission Raftaar is included among these developments, and its work relates to transportation. Mission 41K focuses on energy-efficient solutions that help to have a smaller carbon footprint, and it is set out as a ten-year plan. The Konkan Railway is a 760 km rail route that connects Roha in Maharashtra to Mangalore in Karnataka, and it covers Goa too. The Kolkata Metro Extension is also part of the section, and its line includes a tunnel. The Indian Railways Finance Corporation is another body covered in this section, and it is linked to Indian Railways. The booklet also describes a plan to redevelop major railway stations by working with private companies. These developments are listed under the heading New Development in Indian Railways. The Practice Questions that follow test readers on several of these items, and each item is presented as a separate development in the railway sector.

questions.q: What is the objective of Mission Raftaar?
options: To build the first underwater metro
To set up a private railway station
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Mission Raftaar aims to increase the speed of transportation.

questions.q: Which corporation operates Namo Bharat/RapidX on the Delhi–Ghaziabad–Meerut corridor?
questions.explanation: The booklet says Namo Bharat/RapidX is operated by the National Capital Regional Transport Corporation.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Indian Railways Finance Corporation is the financial arm of Indian Railways.
Reason (R): It was established in 1986.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the year of establishment does not explain why the corporation is the financial arm.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. KAVACH   ->   A. Redevelopment of major railway stations with private companies
II. Namo Bharat/RapidX   ->   B. Automatic Train Protection System
III. Kolkata Metro Extension   ->   C. India's first underwater metro line
IV. Amrit Bharat Station Scheme   ->   D. India's first Rapid Rail
questions.explanation: KAVACH is the Automatic Train Protection System, Namo Bharat/RapidX is India's first Rapid Rail, and the Kolkata Metro Extension is the underwater metro line.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. KAVACH was developed by the Research Design and Standards Organisation.
II. The tunnel of India's first underwater metro line lies beneath the Hooghly River.
III. Mission Raftaar aims to reduce the speed of transportation.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while Statement III reverses the aim of Mission Raftaar.

questions.q: In which year was the Konkan Railway constructed?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the Konkan Railway was constructed in 1998.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Namo Bharat Rapid Rail was earlier known as India's first Vande Metro Train.
II. Indian Railways Finance Corporation was established in 1990.
III. Mission 41K aims to save Rs 41000 crore in 10 years through energy-efficient solutions.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while Statement II gives 1990 instead of 1986.
